column4: @router.put("/") and @router.put(""), status_code=204. On an existing id the handler queries query_statements_by_ids FIRST, then: 🟢 if statements_are_equivalent is FALSE it raises HTTPException(409 CONFLICT, "A different statement already exists with the same ID") and RETURNS BEFORE BACKEND_CLIENT.write is reached. The overwrite never leaves the API process.

column1: PUT
column4: Verbatim source comment: "The LRS specification calls for deep comparison of duplicate statement ids. In the case that the current statement is not equivalent to one found in the database we return a 409, otherwise the usual 204." 🟢 The refusal is DELIBERATE and documented in the code.

column1: PUT
column4: If every existing statement IS equivalent: bare `return`. No write call. 🟢 Idempotent no-op, 204.

column1: POST
column4: Docstring verbatim: "Drop statements already stored; raise on conflicting duplicates." Non-equivalent existing id -> HTTPException(409, "Differing statements already exist with the same ID: {id}"). Equivalent ids are REMOVED from the write set by the closing dict comprehension, so they are never re-indexed.

column4: Atomic batch. After filtering, `if not statements_dict: response.status_code = 204; return None` — an all-duplicate batch writes NOTHING and answers 204.

column1: POST
column4: Opt-in bulk backfill (issue #622). 🔴 Tolerates VALIDATION errors per item but NOT an id conflict: ValueError from the filter -> 409 with PartialSuccessError(index=-1) and inserted_ids=[] — the WHOLE batch is rejected. So "partial success" does not weaken the id guarantee.

column1: # THE GUARANTEE IS IN THE API PROCESS, NOT IN THE STORE, AND THAT IS THE COMMERCIAL POINT.
# p188 measured the other half and it still stands: src/ralph/backends/data/base.py declares
# BaseOperationType {INDEX, CREATE, DELETE, UPDATE, APPEND}, default_operation_type = INDEX
# (which overwrites at a specific id), DELETE is implemented in es.py and exercised in
# mongo.py, and --es-op-type exposes create/index/update/delete as a FIRST-CLASS CLI option.
# SO THE ANSWER SPLITS BY WHO THE ADVERSARY IS:
#   an xAPI CLIENT cannot tamper with a stored statement           -> 409, enforced, free
#   an OPERATOR, a backfill job, or anything holding Elasticsearch
#     or Mongo credentials can delete or overwrite it at will      -> nothing stops it
# CONSEQUENCE FOR PATTERN 32:
#   step 3c (application-layer append-only) is CHEAPER than written — it is already true,
#     and it can be demonstrated to a client in one 409 rather than built.
#   step 3b (the WORM store) STAYS MANDATORY, but its justification CHANGES: it is not
#     there to stop the application, it is there to stop the operator. 🔵 That is the
#     distinction a regulator asks about, and it is a better argument than the one p188 had.
#   The 8-10 week estimate holds, with the weeks moving from 3c to 3b.
